name: Rick’s Café
hero_subtitle: A loving recreation of the bar from the 1942 film, complete with piano, period décor and a refined menu.

overview.title: Of All the Cafés in All the World
overview.p1: There was no real Rick’s Café in the 1942 film — the set was built in Hollywood. Decades later, a former American diplomat opened this restaurant in Casablanca as a careful homage: arched interiors, warm lighting, a grand piano and a menu that mixes international and Moroccan dishes.
overview.p2: It is popular with visitors and locals for special occasions. Reservations are strongly recommended, especially for dinner and weekends. Dress is smart-casual.
overview.p3: Even if you do not eat here, the building and the story make it a stop on many city tours. It sits close to the Old Medina and is an easy taxi ride from the centre or the Corniche.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Rick’s Café

1.title: Reservations
1.desc: Book ahead, especially for dinner and weekends. Walk-ins are not always possible.

2.title: Dress
2.desc: Smart-casual is appropriate. It is a restaurant with a dressy, cinematic mood.

3.title: Getting there
3.desc: Taxi from the centre or Corniche; close to the Old Medina edge.

q1.question: Was there a real Rick’s Café in the film?
q1.answer: No. The film set was in Hollywood. This restaurant is a later homage opened in Casablanca.

q2.question: Do I need a reservation?
q2.answer: Strongly recommended, especially for dinner and weekends.

q3.question: Is it only for tourists?
q3.answer: It draws visitors and locals for special occasions. The atmosphere is polished rather than casual street food.

q4.question: How long should I allow?
q4.answer: About 1.5 to 2 hours for a full meal.

q5.question: What should I combine it with?
q5.answer: Old Medina, Marché Central, or a taxi to the Corniche and Hassan II Mosque.
